articleTitle: A Comprehensive Approach to Wind Turbine Optimization Integrating MPPT and Speed Control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This article presents an in-depth study of wind turbine control strategies that combine Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) techniques using speed control to optimize energy production. Extracting maximum power output from wind turbines requires efficient methods to adapt to varying wind conditions. First, the article reviews conventional MPPT methods, highlighting their advantages but also their limitations when dealing with dynamic wind profiles. Then, an integrated approach is introduced, where speed control is combined with MPPT, with the aim of improving response times and energy capture efficiency. Simulation results show that adding speed control significantly improves wind turbine performance. This results in increased power output through faster response time, dropping from 65 seconds to just 2 seconds. This integrated MPPT-speed control approach thus demonstrates its interest in optimizing power extraction from wind turbines, particularly in variable wind conditions.

articleTitle: Federated Learning-based Healthcare Services for COVID-19 Pandemic
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Healthcare data needs to maintain privacy and security, as it holds sensitive information of patients which can lead to identity theft. In case of centralized data sharing, all the features of data can be seen from the centralized server, thus exploitation of sensitive data can take place. By incorporating decentralized data sharing such as Federated Learning (FL), data privacy and security can be improved as the each component in the FL system contains only parts of data. Privacy will be achieved successfully without any data leakage. This preserves data sovereignty, and could reduce cyber-attacks. Thus, this survey discuses about the COVID-19 prediction using learning techniques by embracing FL in healthcare sector to addresses privacy, security and scalability concerns.

articleTitle: Memristor Crossbar-based String Matching Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient string matching circuit based on a memristor crossbar. It uses a reduced number of memristors compared to the previous string matching circuits. The circuit leverages the computation in memory feature and hence avoids data movement for computation. The proposed circuit is about 1.97x area and energy efficient compared to the previous work. Tuning the conductance of the memristors in the crossbar, a single crossbar circuit can be used for matching strings of different lengths.

articleTitle: Thermal Performance Evaluation Techniques for Thin-Film Semi-Transparent PV Glazing Using Experimental Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Semi-transparent PV glazing is an emerging technology for building integrated photovoltaic applications. Thermal performance evaluation, represented by the overall heat transfer coefficient (U-value) is a key parameter for assessing the suitable of a PV glazing for building façade applications. This work presents three techniques for proper evaluation of the U-value for a cadmium telluride (CdTe) thin-film based semitransparent PV glazing. The advantages of each technique was discussed in light of the obtained results. Results showed that all experiments convey the same U-values of the tested glazing, as the PV glazing has a U-value of 2.67 W/m2K lower than that of the conventional glazing 5.6 W/m2K. Different experiments reveal the results in different profiles in terms of steadiness providing various insights regarding the thermal performance.

articleTitle: Accurate Parameter Determination for Photovoltaic Systems Using Meta-Heuristic Methods: A Comparative Study with Particle Swarm Optimization and Multiple Objective Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: The effective implementation of photovoltaic (PV) systems heavily relies on accurate electrical modeling, where The Single Diode Model (SDM) stands out for its ability to accurately capture the complex behavior of photovoltaic (PV) modules. The SDM involves five unknown parameters, presenting a challenge for precise determination. This study investigates and compares of meta-heuristic methods in addressing this parameter determination challenge. Specifically, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is employed using two distinct objective functions: and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). The validation of these methods is conducted on a PV module provided by RTC FRANCE under standard test conditions (STC). The outcomes of PSO indicate a realistic and accurate determination of the unknown parameters and precise prediction of the I-V curve for the PV module. This research contributes valuable insights into the application of meta-heuristic methods for enhancing the precision and reliability of electrical modeling in PV systems.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of SAC-OCDMA Network Based on 2-D CS Code Utilizing Two Light Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This study introduces a novel 2-dimensional (2D) spectral/temporal code, termed 2D-cyclic shift (2D-CS) code, optimized for non-coherent Spectral Amplitude Coding Optical Code Division Multiple Access (SAC-OCDMA) systems. Computational results demonstrate that the 2D-CS code has fostered the SAC-OCDMA system’s performance whence spectral efficiency (SE), phase induced intensity noise (PIIN), and cardinality. Specifically, the 2D-CS code can increase cardinality by up to 117%, 89%, and 61% compared to one-dimensional CS (1D-CS), 2D-multi service (2D-MS), and 2D-diluted perfect difference (2D-DPD) codes, respectively. The system’s performance was evaluated using Optisystem software, showing significant improvements in quality factor (QF) and bit error rate (BER) with LED and laser light sources for four active users at 115 dBm transmitted power and 20,000 m distance.

articleTitle: Improved Beam Steering Direction in Spiral Antenna Using PIN Diodes for Wireless Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel spiral antenna design capable of generating four steerable beams for wireless communication. The antenna features a central circular disc surrounded by four stubs, with each stub supporting a spiral arm equipped with a PIN diode. A coaxial probe positioned at the center evenly distributes power to the four spiral arms. Operating within the Wi-Fi band at 2.45 GHz, the antenna can achieve four distinct operating states at the same frequency. Beam steering in four directions (0°±, 90°±, 180°±, and 270°±) is achieved by selectively activating and deactivating the PIN diodes. With a peak directivity of 5.79 dBi at 0°±, the antenna offers high performance and precise beam control.

articleTitle: CFD Modeling of Performance of Flat Solar Water Heater for Domestic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Flat plate solar collectors represent a prominent technology in the field of solar thermal energy, specifically designed for residential and commercial water heating applications. This paper provides an overview of flat plate solar collectors and its thermal performance using numerical technique. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) has emerged as a powerful tool for modeling and optimizing flat plate solar collectors, which are crucial for harnessing solar energy in various applications such as residential water heating. This paper analyzes the application of CFD in simulating the fluid dynamics and heat transfer processes within flat solar collectors. It discusses the modeling approaches, including the discretization of governing equations, turbulence modeling techniques, and validation methodologies used to ensure accuracy and reliability of simulations. the key performance parameters such as velocity contours, temperature distributions, and efficiency of flat plate collectors under prescribed operating conditions and geometries are predicted.

articleTitle: Leveraging Spatial and Temporal Features using CNN-LSTM for Improved Bone Fracture Classification from X-ray Images
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: X-ray imaging remains the primary diagnostic tool for identifying bone fractures. Accurate classification of bone fractures from X-ray images is a critical task in the field of orthopedic diagnosis and treatment. However, this task poses several challenges due to the complex and variable nature of fracture patterns, as well as the need to consider the temporal progression of fracture healing. Traditional convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, while effective in extracting spatial features from X-ray images, may not be sufficient to capture the dynamic and sequential aspects of fracture healing. In this work, we propose an improved Convolutional Neural Network-Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) architecture to address the limitations of CNN-only models in bone fracture classification. The proposed method aims to leverage the strengths of both CNNs and LSTMs to enhance the classification performance. The CNN component of the network is responsible for extracting relevant visual features from the X-ray images, while the LSTM layers are used to model the temporal relationships between these features, which are crucial for understanding the progression of fracture healing. Experimental results on a dataset of X-ray images of bone fractures demonstrate the superior performance of the CNN-LSTM architecture compared to traditional CNN-based approaches with 97.33%

articleTitle: Potential, Challenges and Outlook Of Solid State Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Solid state battery is a promising battery technology. It is projected to replace the lithium-ion batteries in the next decade if its critical challenges will be well addressed. The electrodes used in this technology is solid, replacing the liquid electrolyte used in lithium-ion batteries. This paper aims at presenting the state of art of solid-state battery, including its main characteristic, working principle, and manufacturing process. The main benefits and the different challenges facing the wider implementation are discussed in this paper. Solid state battery technology has many benefits compared to lithiumion battery, including higher energy density, improved safety, fast charging time, longer lifetime, and broader working temperatures. Its main challenges are scalability, scarcity of materials used in its manufacturing, recycling difficulties, interface problem, infrastructure, and high manufacturing cost. It is expected that the shifting to mass manufacturing of solid-state batteries will be after 2030.

articleTitle: An Innovative LoRa Based Health-Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has compelled countries worldwide to implement various measures to slow down the spread of the disease and reduce mortality rates. Covid-19 has reassured the need for non-traditional methods to monitor the vital signs and health conditions of patients. Motivated by technological innovations that have rushed to find solutions to besiege the corona virus, our proposal is to create a device capable of monitoring the patient’s vital signs and sending them to a cloud network that includes information about the patient’s identity and location. If vital signs were observed abnormal, an alert is sent to a nearby hospital. Then, the related crew is expected to provide an immediate first aid to the patient. Our proposed technique is not only meant for such worldwide crises, it can also be used for many other purposes, such as monitoring premature babies, and monitoring the elderly who may have multiple diseases and are often exposed to sudden relapses, such as diabetic coma and strokes.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Use of Compressive Sensing on Intelligence Reflecting Surface (IRS) Using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: In this research, the author proposes the use of Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) to increase the signal achievable rate in blind spot conditions, such as in an elevator. IRS is a smart reflective surface that can change the direction of electromagnetic signal reflection. In this case, the author uses a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to optimize the direction of IRS reflections. CNNs can identify patterns and features in data, which in this case is data about signals and the environment around the IRS. By using CNN, the authors were able to develop a model that allows IRS to automatically adjust the direction of signal reflections, which can help in optimizing achievable rate. The aim of this research is to determine the correct direction of IRS reflection and to determine the achievable rate results after using CS and CNN. This research was carried out using Matlab-based simulation using data sets to train and test the system. It is hoped that the implementation of CS and CNN on IRS can increase the signal achievable rate.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Lead-free Perovskite Solar Cells via SCAPS
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)

It is imperative to improve the electrical performance of these flexile and lightweight solar cells for economic and environmental positive impact. The results obtained show that the device performance strongly depends on the absorber layer band-gap. The optimum band-gap for the absorber layer was found to be 1.2 eV. The MoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Cd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>S attained the highest PCE of 25.39 % and 25.31 % respectively, at 1.2 eV. The results imply that MoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Cd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>S are the potential candidates to replace the most commonly used Fluorine-doped Tin Oxide (FTO) and Titanium dioxide (TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) as TCL and ETM to enhance the efficiency of perovskite solar cells.

articleTitle: A Load Balancing Strategy for Enhancing SEC's Power Distribution System Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Transmission line losses pose a significant challenge in power system design and operation, contributing to increased costs and reduced efficiency. This paper introduces an operational method for distribution system networks with multiple electrical sources. By targeting a reduction in transmission line losses, the proposed approach aims to enhance overall power system performance, improve reliability, and lower operational expenses. The strategy's effectiveness is demonstrated through a case study on the Dallah Hospital Namar power system in Saudi Arabia. Results indicate a substantial up to 50% decrease in transmission line losses, leading to reduced operational costs for the Saudi Electricity Company (SEC), mitigated voltage drops, and enhanced system reliability. The proposed methodology holds promise for broader application in power systems with multiple distribution networks.

articleTitle: Solar Potential Assessment for Remote Electrification in Ethiopia: A Comparative Modelling Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Understanding the solar potential of remote regions is crucial for addressing energy poverty, promoting economic development, and mitigating the impacts of climate change, especially in underserved areas. However, access to comprehensive localized solar radiation data is severely limited in most remote regions due to lack of measuring devices and nonfunctional meteorological stations. In this research, we leverage spatially sparse dataset comprising records from 54 sites and meteorological data from 21 sites across Ethiopia, covering 13 years to predict the monthly global solar irradiance (GHI) for remote inaccessible areas where historical data is unavailable. Climatic variables, such as relative sunshine duration and temperatures are used for computing GHI using dual models. To estimate monthly GHI for regions lacking historical data, deterministic inverse distance weighting (IDW) and Geo statistic Kriging cross validation and interpolation techniques have been employed. The analysis results indicated that a solar potential varies from July (3.70 to 6.54) kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/day in March, based on Prescott model, while its value varied from 3.65 to 7.26 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/day in similar months based on Allen model. Our findings revealed that IDW approaches provide a better spatial resolution compared to the Kriging technique. Based on the mean per months bases Statistical error model analysis exhibited accurate, reliable, and outstanding performance, showcasing minimal Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) values of 0.15, 0.21, and 0.05, along with Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) values of 0.29, 0.83, and 0.79 for the Kriging technique applied to sunshine, temperature and NASA respectively. This study's solar radiation predictions offer crucial insights for off-grid design, policy development, and sustainable rural electrification.

articleTitle: Estimating Household’s Energy Consumption of Summer Cooling in Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: The residential sector is anticipated to account for approximately two-thirds of the total energy demand, with a significant portion of domestic electricity consumption attributed to air conditioning. In Saudi Arabia and other GCC region, a major challenge lies in decreasing electricity consumption and enhancing energy efficiency and hence reduce household’s electricity bills. Consequently, it is imperative to examine and measure consumption trends associated with various activities. In this paper, a technique was proposed to estimate the electrical energy used for air conditioning per household, and choose eastern province in Saudi Arabia as a case study. The methodology uses electricity data gathered from the monthly electricity bill for households and daily temperatures in eastern province. It has been estimated that 45 to 60% of electrical energy is used for cooling during May to October months. The results from this study underscore the need for both technological advancements in cooling systems and behavioral changes to reduce energy consumption during the hot summer months.

articleTitle: An Efficient Method for Big Data Classification using Optimized Error-Minimized and Ridge-Regression ELM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: A parallelized learning algorithm called Extreme Learning Machine tree (ELM) is used to classify the data instances more effectively in big data analysis. In ELM Tree approach, the over-partitioning problem in Decision Tree (DT) generation is resolved by using ELM as a leaf node when the information gain ratio or ambiguity of available cuts are smaller than a specified threshold. However, perturbation, multicollinearity, and stability are other shortcomings that constrain the performance of ELM. This research proposes an Optimized Error-minimized and Ridge-regression Extreme Learning Machine (OER-ELM) to address those challenges. In OER-ELM, the required number of hidden nodes during learning stage is incremented to obtain minimum error. The least-square method-based output weight calculation is replaced by ridge-regression. The initially chosen input weights and hidden biases of ELM are typically selected at random. This work proposes techniques for optimization such as Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Firefly (FF) algorithm to modify the input weights and hidden biases. The experiment is conducted for GA- ELM Tree, GA-OER-ELM Tree, PSO-ELM Tree, PSO-OER-ELM Tree, FF-ELM Tree and FF-OER-ELM Tree on three big datasets. Based on the results of the experiments, it was determined that OER-ELM Tree is superior to ELM Tree in terms of classification accuracy and computing efficiency.

Author Keywords: Optimized Error -Minimized and Ridge-Regression Extreme Learning Machine

articleTitle: A Performance Analysis of Building Integrated PV Systems in Jordanian Residential Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Photovoltaic panels are becoming a popular renewable energy source for homes. However, some houses have limited space for installing the system. Building integrated photovoltaic are promising technologies for such cases. This study suggests a new semi-transparent PV panel design to be installed on a 100 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>façade house to satisfy the power demand throughout the year. Results show that the proposed system can cover 84.8% of the total energy consumption while considering the limited space on the façade. The new PV panel design reduces light energy consumption by 30%. The proposed system is feasible, with a payback period of 4.4 years and a reduction in total carbon emissions by 4.46 tons.

articleTitle: A GRO metaheuristic algorithm for Parameters identification of a single diode in a photovoltaic model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: The identification of parameters for photovoltaic (PV) models as an optimization problem has garnered significant interest in the scientific literature. In this context, this article explores the performance of the Gold Rush Optimizer (GRO) algorithm for extracting the parameters of the single-diode model. To this end, we evaluated the GRO's ability to extract all parameters of the single-diode model of the R.T.C. solar cell, using the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and standard deviation (std) as performance measures. The performance of the GRO was compared with other algorithms such as JAYA and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results show that our algorithm achieves the lowest Root Mean Square Error of 9.8602E-04 and the lowest standard deviation of 9.4593E-14. These results demonstrate that this optimization approach outperforms competing methods in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and stability. Thus, the GRO method proves to be particularly effective and reliable for the accurate estimation of PV model parameters.

articleTitle: Redistribution and management of stored energy in electric vehicles for grid integration
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This work presents a multifunctional chain for the redistribution of solar energy integrated in the single-phase grid in parallel with a non-linear load. This process is carried out using bidirectional converters and supported by the energy stored in electric vehicle’s battery. The principle of extracting the maximum power produced by the solar panel is implemented by the Maximum Power Point Tracking’s InC algorithm. The duty cycle managing the switching sequences of the bidirectional DC-DC converter is generated by the Generalized Predictive Control (GPC) while the non-linear load inserted in the chain is identified using robust bias-compensated normalized maximum correntropy criterion (BCNMCC). Based on the latter method and the equivalent parameters of the battery and solar panel, a single-phase inverter control is performed. In the case of grid-connected power generation, a synchronization unit, namely the phase-locked loop (PLL), is indispensable in such a system. All the performances are evaluated in V2G and G2V modes on MATLAB/SIMULINK platform.

Author Keywords: robust bias-compensated normalized maximum correntropy criterion

articleTitle: Sub-6 GHz Beam-Switched Array Antenna for Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This study introduces the design and development of a beam-switching array antenna for sub-6 GHz wireless communication applications. The proposed design includes four rectangular radiating cells positioned above a rectangular ground plane and fed by a microstrip line. The antenna elements are powered through mutual coupling. The main beam direction can be adjusted by switching four PIN diodes on or off, allowing the beam to be steered in the azimuthal plane at angles of 55°, 125°, 235°, and 305°. The simulation results show a steering capability of 40° in the XZ-plane (ϕ = 0°), ranging from -20° to +20°, and a 50° steering range in the YZ-plane (ϕ = 90°), also from -25° to +25°. For all operating states, the bandwidth is 9.86%. The proposed antenna achieves a peak gain of 7.74 dBi and maintains high efficiency, between 75% and 84%, over the 5.41 GHz to 5.97 GHz operating band. Furthermore, reconfiguring the radiation pattern also enhances gain, bandwidth, and efficiency.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Random Forest and Decision Tree Classifiers for Predicting Type 2 Diabetes using K-Fold Cross-Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This study investigates the prediction accuracy of type 2 diabetes using the Pima-Indians-Diabetes dataset, employing a novel classifier that integrates Random Forest and K-fold cross-validation. Additionally, the findings are compared with predictions obtained from a Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) classifier. The dataset, consisting of 768 samples, was used for both training and testing. Using a significance level of α=0.05 and power=0.80 in the G*Power analysis, the results consistently approached an accuracy of 80%. The Decision Tree classifier achieved an accuracy of 86.245%, while the novel Random Forest classifier outperformed it with an accuracy of 96.179%. An Independent Samples T-Test yielded a p-value of 0.01 (p<0.05), indicating a statistically significant relationship between the performance of the Random Forest classifier, K-fold cross-validation, and the Decision Tree classifier. Overall, the Random Forest classifier demonstrated superior predictive accuracy, highlighting its effectiveness in type 2 diabetes prediction.

articleTitle: Hands-on Experiential Learning of Machine Learning Concepts Through Senior Design Projects: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Introducing machine learning (ML) concepts to undergraduate electrical engineering students through senior design projects is a practical and effective method for hands-on learning. This approach enables students to apply AI/ML techniques to real-world engineering challenges, helping them gain valuable interdisciplinary skills and preparing them for the increasing demand for ML expertise in the industry. Senior design projects offer an informal way to introduce AI/ML without needing a dedicated course, fostering problem-solving abilities and enhancing career readiness. This paper presents a case study of teaching ML concepts through their application in senior design projects in the electrical engineering department at Prince Mohammad University, Saudi Arabia. This strategy ensures that students graduate with the essential ML skills needed to thrive in the evolving technological landscape. Results from a student survey illustrates the pros and cons of this approach and it highlights several key insights relevant to this case study, showcasing the positive impact of integrating AI/ML projects into the students' educational experience.

articleTitle: Simulating Enhanced Rigid Body Orientation Estimation in Space through Implementation of Fusion Algorithms Using IMU Data
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This manuscript is centered on the estimation of the attitude of a body evolving in a 3D space. In this context, the chosen representation of attitude is the Euler angle method, and the accessible measurement data come only from an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) that comprising a triad of triaxial proprioceptive sensors (3 Accelerometers and 3 Gyrometers). The objective of this research is to study and implement inertial data fusion methods by combining measurements from an IMU to visualize the orientation of mobile body. Numerical simulations as well as experiments using real data have validated all implemented methods.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy Assessment: A Comparative Study of Saudi Arabia and Greensboro-NC
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This paper comprehensively assesses wind and solar energy potential in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA), focusing on five strategically selected locations: Al-Ahsa, Riyadh, Rafha, Tabuk, and Unayzah. The analysis was extended, and a comparison was made between the results of the investigated locations in KSA and the city of Greensboro North Carolina State in USA. The study aims to estimate the amount of energy that can be extracted from wind and solar resources, leveraging advance d computational tools for precise evaluation. The "Distribution Fitter" app in MATLAB was utilized to fit the parameters of the used probability density functions PDFs. In parallel, the RETScreen software was utilized to estimate the annual extractable energy from solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, offering a reliable simulation of solar irradiance and system performance. Greensboro stands out as the most promising site for wind energy extraction with an annual amount of 21,022.02 MWh by 10 Vestas turbines, while Al-Ahsa demonstrates the highest potential for solar energy harvesting with an annual estimated amount of 257.426 MWh by a 100 kW PV system. This dual-resource assessment highlights the regional variability in renewable energy potential across KSA, emphasizing the importance of site-specific analysis for optimal energy resource utilization. The results serve as a valuable reference for policymakers and stakeholders in the renewable energy sector, guiding future investments and development plans toward sustainable energy solutions in the region.

articleTitle: PID – loopshaping controller design for reference tracking of a second – order, open – loop system
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This paper introduces a Proportional, Integral, Derivative (PID) controller architecture for reference tracking of a linear system whose dynamics are described by a second – order, transfer function. The proposed controller architecture facilitates the design and the analysis of the control algorithm by utilizing concepts from three popular controller design methods, namely PID controller design, Loop – shaping controller design and Feedback Linearization. The equivalence of the three controller design methods, when using the proposed controller architecture, provides useful insights to the control designer in choosing the parameters of the PID controller in a systematic way. An application of the controller design method is presented in order to explain the rationale in choosing the controller parameters.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis of Floating and Conventional Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems are increasingly popular worldwide and present a promising avenue for renewable energy generation. Despite their benefits, conventional solar power plants face several challenges related to installation and operation. In response, floating photovoltaic (FPV) systems have been developed to mitigate the environmental impact associated with traditional PV setups. Floating PV systems, deployed on water surfaces, provide several benefits compared to traditional land-based PV installations. These advantages include better cooling due to the water surface, more efficient land use, and potential synergistic interactions with aquatic ecosystems. Over the past decade, the FPV market has expanded rapidly, with global installed capacity doubling annually. This study performs an in-depth comparative analysis of the power output from floating and conventional solar PV systems, with a primary focus on evaluating their power generation efficiency. This research utilizes the MATLAB/Simulink platform to simulate the entire system, modifying the standard photovoltaic power generation model to accommodate the FPV configuration. By analyzing data from current installations and conducting simulation-based evaluations, the study demonstrates that floating solar PV systems achieve higher energy yields, attributed to enhanced cooling effects and minimized shading

articleTitle: Improving Sensitivity And Selectivity of Breast Cancer Detection Systems Through the Development of a High-Performance LNA
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This paper describes the development of a planar low-noise amplifier (LNA) using InGaAs-HEMT technology, which is compact and features a high figure of merit, intended for breast cancer detection systems. A resistive termination topology was chosen, combined with a cascade configuration, offering perfect input-output matching over a frequency range of 1.87 to 3.5 GHz. This frequency band is used for detecting smaller tumors. The designed amplifier provides an average S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> gain of 27.66 dB with low ripple of 1.23 dB, a noise figure (NF) ranging from 2.02 dB to 2.56 dB, perfect isolation of 54.96 dB, and a compact size of 31 x 22.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The LNA also exhibits a group delay (GD) of (0.461 ± 0.103) ns, a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 60.7 %, and a figure of merit (FOM) of 174. The linearity of the amplifier was also studied, showing an average input compression point IP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> of - 12.52 dBm and a third-order input intercept point (IIP3) of 10 dBm. These performances enhance the selectivity and sensitivity of cancer detection systems.

articleTitle: Advanced Optimized Active Cell Balancing with Efficient Power Electronics Algorithms for Superior Battery Performance in Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Effective battery cell balancing is critical for achieving optimal performance and safety in modern energy storage systems. This work investigates active balancing techniques, which leverage power electronic controllers to enhance battery pack performance beyond the capabilities of passive methods. The system integrates DC-DC converters and bidirectional power transfer circuits to facilitate efficient energy management. Real-time voltage and state of charge monitoring allow precise power flow adjustment, while advanced algorithms provide sophisticated decision-making and control. This approach minimises State of charge disparities, maximises usable capacity, and extends battery lifespan. Additionally, active balancing reduces thermal stress and mitigates safety risks, positioning it as a valuable technology for applications such as electric vehicles and renewable energy storage. Active balancing is pivotal in advancing sustainable energy solutions by improving energy efficiency and lowering costs.

articleTitle: Contribution to the Development of a Multifunctional Planar Filter Based on SMV-1405 Diodes for 5G Mobile Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative structure of a multifunctional filter mounted on a 0.8 mm thick Roger 4003C substrate. The developed filter can flexibly adjust its bandwidth, ranging from narrowband to wideband and vice versa. Additionally, the optimal arrangement of the SMV1405 diodes allows the filter to switch from a single-band configuration to a dual-band configuration while maintaining a narrow bandwidth. The results obtained are promising, with a return loss S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> of 33 dB and an insertion loss S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> of 0.94 dB in narrowband mode. In dual-band mode, it produces two narrow bands with return losses greater than 15 dB and insertion losses less than 1.74 dB.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of P&O and ANN MPPT Algorithms in Conventional and Floating Solar Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) has proven to be the most reliable source of solar energy production. The performance of PV systems depends on sunlight and temperature, which fluctuate throughout the day. This results in fluctuations in the maximum power point (MPP) on the performance curve of the photovoltaic system. Therefore, various Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) techniques are used to track the MPP and extract maximum performance from the photovoltaic system. The paper presents a comparative analysis of perturb and observe (P&O) maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and artificial neural network (ANN) algorithms in conventional and floating solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. The study assesses the performance and effectiveness of these algorithms in varying environmental conditions. Simulations are carried out in the MATLAB/Simulink environment. The results show that ANN performs better than R&D in both systems in this study.

articleTitle: Evaluation Of The Thermal Management Efficiency Of a Heat Sink For Electronic Devices Under Transient Heat Flux Shock
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This paper examines the evaluation of thermal control performance of a heat sink designed for an electronic device subjected to transient heat flux shock. Its primary objective is to assess the efficacy of thermal management in mitigating the impact of sudden thermal shocks on electronic devices. Thermal control effectiveness is examined by minimizing peak temperatures, enhancing natural convection, optimizing heat transfer with ambient air, and ensuring overall temperature regulation efficiency. The findings indicate that employing a heat sink with triangular fins and phase change material leads to a reduction in maximum temperature by 10 K compared to a heat sink with rectangular fins. Achieving peak thermal efficiency is possible when the phase-altering substance envelops the triangular fins completely. With a combination of PCM and triangular fins, exceptional temperature control efficiency can be attained.

articleTitle: Intelligent Solar Power Forecast with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Solar power forecast is a necessity for efficient operation of Smart Grids for good energy management. Before forecasting any data related to solar power, it is important to gather precise data related to several aspects of solar irradiance; which being the main input for generation of solar power. Globally, solar radiation forecasting is performed by several methods, two of them main methods being cloud imagery combined with physical models, and machine learning models. The objective of this paper is to provide an overview of the building of machine learning models for the forecasting of solar power from historical data and how the use of libraries like XGBoost can improve scalability and accuracy in prediction. A few of the recent works on solar irradiance forecasting using other approaches include Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Deep Learning can also be utilised for very precise forecasting. In further studies, different approaches can be compared to figure out the ideal approach to build a model for this specific task. This paper also covers certain aspects of artificial neural networks and how they are the building blocks of this particular machine learning model.

articleTitle: Towards a Smart Learning Environment : A Model for Smart Education using IoT and AI
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Smart education has become a hallmark of information and communication technology in education (ICTE). The continuous introduction of new technologies into learning environments aims to enable learners to develop and enhance their skills, leading to improved learning outcomes. Technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), Generative AI, and mobile technology are among the latest to be integrated into educational infrastructures and systems. These smart technologies offer personalized content creation, automate administrative tasks, and enhance student engagement through adaptive interactions. However, despite the promising benefits, challenges such as security and privacy concerns, the need for robust infrastructure, and ongoing technical support must be addressed. This paper proposes a comprehensive model for implementing smart education technologies, addressing these challenges. The proposed model serves as a blueprint for educational institutions aiming to leverage modern technologies to create smarter, more efficient learning environments.

articleTitle: A Review of Solar Energy Applications in Transportation Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: The importance of solar energy as an alternative to traditional fossil fuel vehicles in addressing increasing population and transportation demands while reducing pollution. It emphasizes the use of solar-powered vehicles, which convert sunlight into electricity through photovoltaic cells, offering a sustainable solution. Ongoing research aims to enhance the efficiency of capturing, converting, and storing solar energy to make solar cars more competitive. It introduces the concept of a Solar-Powered Electric Vehicle (SPEV) that utilizes a battery charged by photovoltaic panels and external power sources, integrating advanced technologies for optimal power generation. The passage analyzes the performance of solar-powered cars, covering various aspects including energy calculation, battery modeling, and environmental impact comparison with conventional vehicles. A life cycle cost analysis evaluates the economic feasibility of solar cars.

articleTitle: Evaluate properties of Bell-based Frobenius-Sigmoid polynomials and applications in computer modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: The main focus of this investigation is the applications of Sigmoid functions. Due to its various uses in physics, engineering, and computer science, we introduce Bell-based Frobenius-Sigmoid polynomials and numbers. With the help of generating functions and their functional equations, we derive some properties of these types of polynomials and numbers. Furthermore, we derive symmetric identities for the Bell-based Frobenius-Sigmoid numbers and polynomials. Lastly, we present graphical representations and analyze the zeros of the Bell-based Frobenius-Sigmoid polynomials utilizing computational methods.

articleTitle: IoT and WSN-based Smart Parking Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Rapid urbanization has intensified the strain on existing parking infrastructure, necessitating innovative approaches for efficient and sustainable urban mobility. This paper addresses the escalating parking challenges in urban areas worldwide by proposing a cutting-edge solution leveraging Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) technology and Internet of Things (IoT). The proposed system deploys WSN-based smart sensors in parking spaces to revolutionize parking management. These sensors facilitate real-time data collection, analysis, and communication, enabling a dynamic and adaptive parking system. Through mobile applications, users gain instant access to information about available parking spots, optimizing their search and reducing congestion. Beyond addressing immediate parking scarcity challenges, the proposed solution contributes to the development of smarter, more accessible, and environmentally conscious urban environments. As cities grapple with the complexities of rapid urbanization, the adoption of WSN-based parking solutions emerges as a scalable strategy to create efficient, accessible, and sustainable urban spaces. This project seeks to pave the way for a transformative shift in the global approach to urban mobility through the implementation of intelligent and connected parking solutions.

articleTitle: A comparative analysis between different magnetic couplers for inductive power transfer-based electric vehicles charging
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: The expanding Electric vehicle (EV) market is fuelled by the need for more efficient and dependent ways to recharge the battery. The Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) methodology eliminates the drawbacks and risks associated with the conventional conductive system by eradicating the necessity for direct physical interaction between vehicles and charge equipment. The innovative WPT technique replaces the conductive charging system to keep a similar power rating and efficiency. Numerous strategies have been created to improve the effectiveness and dependability of the WPT model. In this work, we compared two charging methods: one charging through a single transmitter track and the other through a segmented transmitter track. The designs of the 3D models of the coils were made on Ansys. On this software, we tested the effectiveness of inductive charge couplers. This comparison allows us to choose the best type of charging coupler to recharge the battery of the Electric Vehicle.

articleTitle: Smart Shopping Cart With Machine Learning, Navigation, and Weighing Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: The supermarket shopping experience in Saudi Arabia has faced significant challenges, such as long checkout queues, inefficient weighing processes for fruits and vegetables, and the lack of real-time product tracking. These issues lead to customer dissatisfaction and hinder operational efficiency in supermarkets. To address these challenges, our Smart Shopping Cart project was developed, incorporating advanced technologies to streamline and enhance the shopping experience. The Smart Cart integrates a machine learning-based camera recognition system for automatic item identification. Additionally, it features a precise weighing system for fruits and vegetables, providing real-time weight measurements directly within the cart. The inclusion of real-time position tracking further enhances convenience by enabling customers to easily locate items within the store. Lastly, a user-friendly graphical interface displays product details, total cost, and allows for seamless interaction. By integrating these innovative technologies, our Smart Shopping Cart improves customer satisfaction and help retailers optimize their operations. This paper presents the design, implementation, and performance evaluation of the Smart Shopping Cart system, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize the retail industry by addressing contemporary shopping challenges.

articleTitle: Fourier Synchrosqueezed Transform When Used for Medical OCT Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: A projection scheme in the Fourier domain is proposed to suppress speckle noise in Optical Computed Tomography (OCT) images. A comparison is held between the discrete fast Fourier transform (FFT) and the discrete Fourier synchrosqueezed transform (FSST) through two hard thresholding techniques; the projection of signal space onto the noisy subspace in the frequency domain, and the selection of large magnitude coefficients from the spectrum. Results show the efficacy of the Fourier transform compared to the Fourier synchrosqueezed transform, and that is through the projection method over the selection of large magnitude coefficients method. When applied to simulated and real OCT images, and in terms of numerical and visual assessment, the proposed scheme has outperformed benchmark schemes used in the area of OCT image despeckling, such as Total Variation (TV) filter, Geometric Non-Linear Diffusion (GNLD) filter and Detail Preserving Anisotropic Diffusion (DPAD) filter.

articleTitle: Virtual Jamming Attacks Detection Using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), in recent times, have become one of the most promising network solutions with a wide range of applications in agriculture, health and military environments. Despite these promising applications, sensor nodes in WSN are vulnerable to security attacks, one of which is virtual jamming. The goal of this report is to develop a system that can protect data from virtual jamming attacks using neural networks technology. To evaluate the performance of the proposed system, the confusion matrix is used as the main evaluation tool. The confusion matrix will make it possible to measure the extent to which the system is able to distinguish between normal conditions and virtual jamming attacks. Evaluation of the level of detection accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 value is carried out to provide an in- depth understanding of the effectiveness of the system.

articleTitle: Q-eBall: A Hybrid Physical Electronic Game for the Next Generation of Bubble Soccer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: The widespread of electronic games has increased screen time, causing negative consequences such as autism, social isolation, vision problems, and back pain. This underscores the need for new games that blend physical activity with digital engagement. Consequently, the field of physically interactive electronic games has emerged, driven by advancements in sensor technology. In response, we present a novel hybrid physical electronic game, named Q-eBall. It builds upon the traditional bubble soccer game by replacing the real physical ball, which was causing a level of mundanity in the game, with a visual ball. This visual electronic ball is a group of integrated Light-Emitting Diodes (LEDs) in the players’ plastic bumper bubbles. The game incorporates an embedded electronic circuit, a keypad for precise visual ball transfers, and sensors for detecting player falls and scoring. A centralized game server manages communication, monitors player status, and ensures smooth gameplay progression. The electronic integration in Q-eBall adds a new dimension of complexity, opening up possibilities for unique gameplay strategies and tactical choices. This paper describes the concept of Q-eBall game, along with a prototype and offers a labeled dataset collected from accelerometer, gyroscope, and pressure sensor during gameplay. The dataset comprises 173 falls and 206 non-fall events across 15 gameplay sessions, making it a valuable resource for researchers interested in analyzing and evaluating fall detection algorithms.

articleTitle: Cyber-Attack Detection in Smart Grids: A Comparative Analysis of Supervised and Semi-Supervised Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: The advancement of smart grids has addressed many challenges of traditional power grids, yet it has also introduced new vulnerabilities to cyber-attacks that can disrupt power, leading to severe socio-economic impacts like blackouts and grid disturbance. While numerous supervised machine learning methods have been proposed to detect cyber-attacks in smart grids, they require a large dataset of normal and attack instances for training. However, gathering sufficient samples of diverse attack scenarios, especially zero-day attacks, is challenging. In this paper, we develop a semi-supervised model to detect grid attacks using phasor measurement unit (PMU) data from a power system dataset. Principal component analysis (PCA) is applied to select optimal components, and the model is trained using high instances of normal event data, thus enabling it to identify new, unknown attack patterns. We also developed a supervised model for comparison, evaluating both using key metrics. Results demonstrate that the semi-supervised model is more effective in detecting attack events (with 91.2% precision and 90% accuracy) than the supervised approach (90.7% precision and 91.8% accuracy).

Index Terms: Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve

articleTitle: Simulating and Evaluating the Performance of a Cloud Computing Datacenter Using Queuing Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Cloud computing and virtualization are fundamental to modern computer system design. As cloud computing adoption grows across organizations, evaluating its performance becomes essential. This study simulates and analyzes a cloud datacenter’s performance using queuing models. Specifically, an M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>/M/1/K queuing system is employed, with arrival parameters estimated from real CPU utilization data from the Bitbrains datacenter, modeled as discrete Homogeneous Poisson Processes (HPPs). The simulation results of the modeled system reveal minimal average waiting time and efficient task processing with low delays. Additionally, the study highlights the significant impact of service rates on the average response times of tasks arriving as discrete HPPs. These findings offer valuable insights into cloud datacenter performance, aiding in informed decisions for service upgrades and optimal resource utilization.

articleTitle: Solar Energy Forecasting using Optimized Attention-based Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Solar energy is abundantly available in the environment and is beneficial for preserving the environment, since they are regenerative and hold significant promise for the future. Forecasting accurate solar energy plays a major part in enhancing the determination of solar power plants, while also decreasing reliance on fossil fuels for economic and social progress. In the domain of deep learning (DL), the prediction of solar resources has transitioned from traditional statistical methods to the implementation of advanced DL models. This work introduces a model of "optimized attention-bidirectional long short-term memory" (OA-Bi-LSTM) for predicting solar energy. Here, the hyper-parameters of the BiLSTM are optimized by the manta ray optimization (MRO). The proposed model predicts solar energy in an efficient manner with respect to the different measures and achieves better MAE (0.15) and RMSE (0.21) values respectively.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Classification from MRI Scans using a Custom 4-Residual Deep Learning Architecture and Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Computer aided diagnostic (CAD) are used by radiologists and medical specialists to classify brain tumors from machine generated magnetic resonance image (MRI). Acquisition mechanisms of these images reduces quality of images and therefore sometimes leads to misclassification of the brain tumor. This problem arises a need to develop techniques that can classify brain tumors of different types (i.e. glioma, meningioma and pituitary) with better accuracy. A new automated architecture is proposed in this work for brain tumor classification. A statistical method is employed first to enhance the contrast, then sparse autoencoder based data augmentation is performed. A novel 4RDL-DCNN deep learning network is proposed and trained on the selected MRI dataset. Features are extracted from the global average pool layer of the designed model and further optimized using a nature inspired particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. A famous Figshare brain tumor MRI dataset (publically available) is used to conduct experiments. The obtained accuracy of 98.60% is achieved on this dataset that is improved, then the compared to techniques in the literature.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Physiological Signal Processing and Classification: Advances in EEG, EMG, and EOG Modalities
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG), Electromyogram (EMG), and Electrooculogram (EOG) are crucial biomedical signals that present particulars of brain activity, muscle activity, and eye movements which are useful in many critical domains like clinical diagnosis and assistive technologies. The intention of this review article is investigate on the data collection of these physiological signals, analyze available datasets, and provide insights into the state of the art techniques available along with offering possible directions for future work.

articleTitle: Solar Energy Prediction Using Complementary EEMD and Optimum Least Square-Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Accurate solar energy prediction is adequate for the robust combination of solar power into the energy grid, optimizing energy management, and reducing reliance on nonrenewable resources. This work integrates the Complementary Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (CEEMD) and optimum Least Square-Support Vector Machine (OLS-SVM) for accurate solar energy prediction. Initially, the dataset is pre-processed by the cubic spline interpolation (CSI). The CEEMD is presented for extracting the non-stationary and non-linear solar energy time-series data into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), isolating different frequency components and reducing noise. These IMFs are fed as input features for the OLS-SVM, a robust machine learning (ML) model that can manage computational efficiency and capacity to handle nonlinear relationships. Here, the optimal process is done by the rat optimizer (RO) The LS-SVM is trained and optimized to predict future solar energy values based on the extracted features. The suggested CEEMD-OLS-SVM approach provided better MSE (0.2) and RMSE (0.3) in solar energy prediction compared to conventional ML models. By utilizing the strengths of both CEEMD and OLS-SVM, this method provides a reliable tool to improve solar energy prediction and enhance the robustness of solar energy utilization.

articleTitle: Diabetes Mellitus Classification Using Machine Learning Algorithms with Hyperparameter Tuning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Diabetes Mellitus is a prevalent condition globally, marked by elevated blood sugar levels resulting from either insufficient production of insulin or the body cells' inability to respond appropriately to released insulin. For people with diabetes to lead healthy, normal lives, early identification and treatment of the condition are essential. With the need to move away from current traditional procedures, towards a noninvasive methodology, machine learning and data mining technologies can be very useful in the classification of diabetes. Creating an effective machine learning model for the classification of diabetes mellitus was the primary goal of this research. This work is primarily carried out on combined Pima Indian diabetes dataset and German Frankfurt diabetes dataset. The class imbalance issue has been resolved using Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique. One-hot encoding is applied to convert categorial features to numerical and various single and ensemble classifiers with the best hyperparameters obtained using GridSearchCV method were employed on the pre-processed dataset. With an AUC of 0.98 and maximum accuracy of 98.79%, the Random Forest ensemble technique outperformed the other models, according to the experimental results. As a result, the algorithm might be used to predict diabetes and alert doctors to serious cases that call for emergency care.

articleTitle: Arabic Offense Text Detection in Social Networks using Collaborative Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: In an era of abundant social media use and digital communication, the classification of Arabic social media content and user comments into relevant categories poses a significant challenge. The content in social network platforms often encompasses a wide range of topics, sentiments, and societal concerns, making it essential to develop effective methods for discerning and categorizing these expressions. In this research, a new dataset for Arabic offensive text is built along with the methodology proposed for classifying Arabic content into five categories collected from different social networking sites. Leveraging a diverse array of text representation techniques, including TF-IDF, Bag of Words (BoW), custom embeddings, and pre-trained embeddings from models such as Arabert and Mbert, a comprehensive evaluation is conducted based, shedding light on the optimal approach for tackling this complex problem. The findings reveal that the TF-IDF and BoW methods stand out with an impressive 89% accuracy, emphasizing their robustness in addressing the nuances of Arabic tweet classification across these sensitive topics. This study offers valuable insights into the challenges inherent in categorizing Arabic social media content, emphasizing the significance of the TF-IDF approach as an effective tool for this task.

articleTitle: A Novel Hydroponic Based on Hybrid Renewable Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Hydroponic farming, a soilless technique, has become increasingly popular and is considered the future of agriculture in water-deficient areas like Saudi Arabia. These regions tackle the challenge of cultivating fruits and vegetables with an automated hydroponic system. This system uses ozone filtration, is self-installed, and includes PV, DG, battery, converter, and AI for independent functioning. It employs ozonic methods to cleanse and filter water, eliminating the need for human intervention, and offers customizable options to accommodate various locations. The proposed hydroponic system will use sensors as input and output devices, run on a hybrid renewable energy system (HRES), and integrate water pumps, dosing pumps, and lighting sources. By integrating solar panels, batteries, converters, and a diesel generator (DG), the goal is to decrease CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions, water, and power usage, and utilize AI for disease detection. This cutting-edge system tackles multiple challenges in hydroponic agriculture, such as sporadic solar energy, efficient energy storage, converter performance, and diesel generator emissions, aiming to reduce energy wastage and emissions while maintaining dependable operation. The proposed design method assesses the energy needs for growing hydroponic lettuce, cutting down on water and energy usage by decreasing the water pump’s running time to only 4 hours instead of 24 hours. This results in a 40% reduction in energy and cost savings with the ideal sizes of PV, battery, DG, and converter. The system, utilizing HOMER and GAMS software, presents cost and energy savings and operational expense reductions, offering advantages for business owners, agricultural enthusiasts, and individuals looking into agricultural investments. This system could boost local investment in agriculture and technology sectors, in line with Saudi Vision 2030.

articleTitle: Development of a Multi-Functional Smart Helmet for Enhanced Rider Safety and Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This paper describes the design and development of a Smart Helmet Technology (SHT) that integrates multi-sensor monitoring and communication technologies to enhance the motorcycle rider safety. After rigorous testing of the individual components, followed by the integration and 3D printing of electronics box, the final design is thoroughly evaluated in real-world conditions. It was found that the product is reliable in detecting accidents, monitoring health parameters, and sending emergency alerts with precise location data. Moreover, during testing, it was indicated that the proposed smart helmet not only addresses the gaps in previous designs but also aligns with the third United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG 3) as it promotes health and well-being via innovative technology use. Therefore, our smart helmet offers a comprehensive solution to motorcycle safety, by potentially reducing injuries and improving emergency response times in case of accidents.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimal power flow with wind-solar-small hydro power using non-dominated sorting genghis khan shark optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: In this paper, an enhanced version of the Non-dominated Sorting Genghis Khan Shark Optimizer (NSGKSO) is proposed to tackle complex multi-objective optimization problems, with a specific focus on the Optimal Power Flow (OPF) problem. The optimization incorporates renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, and small-hydro power, which introduce significant variability and complexity into the system. The proposed NSGKSO is based on the widely used NSGA-II framework but incorporates novel mechanisms to improve convergence and solution diversity. We evaluated the performance of NSGKSO on several OPF test cases and compared its results with other state-of-the-art algorithms. Our experimental results demonstrate that NSGKSO achieves a better balance between convergence speed and diversity preservation, making it well-suited for solving multi-objective OPF problems in the presence of renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: AI-driven Natural Language Processing: ChatGPT's Potential and Future Advancements in Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: This research paper delves into the operational mechanisms, strengths, and future potential of ChatGPT, an intelligent chatbot developed by OpenAI. ChatGPT's architecture, rooted in the transformer model, enables it to generate contextually relevant text using attention mechanisms and tokenisation. While excelling in generative capability and versatility, the paper highlights challenges, including context understanding and sensitivity to phrasing, sparking discussions on refinement strategies. The study explores opportunities for efficient, prompt engineering, emphasising tokenization strategies to optimise interactions within ChatGPT's token limits. Future advancements envision enhanced context understanding, reduced sensitivity to phrasing, and ethical considerations, addressing verbosity and response diversity concerns. A comparative analysis with competing models like Google's Bard and Meta's LLaMA provides insights into their architectures, parameters, strengths, weaknesses, and target use cases. The paper concludes by emphasising ChatGPT's transformative impact on AI, shaping a future marked by interdisciplinary applications, ethical considerations, and user-centric design.

articleTitle: Project-Based Learning Approach for Undergraduate Electrical Engineering Laboratories: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Teaching undergraduate electrical engineering laboratories with disconnected or disjointed experiments presents several disadvantages, including fragmented learning, limited real-world application, and inefficient skill development. Students may struggle with understanding system integration, teamwork, and the engineering design process. A project-based learning (PBL) approach wherein a connected series of experiments that culminates in a comprehensive project can provide a more cohesive, practical, and engaging learning experience, better preparing students for the complexities of real-world engineering challenges. In this paper, we present a case study of applying PBL approach in the teaching of Microcontroller Systems Lab in the department of Electrical Engineering at Prince Mohammad bin Fahd University (PMU), Saudi Arabia. Students taking this lab work on a series of experiments to build a robotic car with multiple functions. Survey results are presented that validate the effectiveness of this approach.

articleTitle: Face Recognition using SIFT and LBPH-based Hybrid Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: The face recognition has been focused on object detection from images using various deep learning and machine learning models. This work proposes a deep learning model using multiple testing platforms to identify different face images from either videos or images. Two feature extraction methods, Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT) and Local Binary Patterns Histogram (LBPH) and a deep learning model (ResNet) is considered in the proposed model. LBPH features and ResNet models are considered for face recognition through videos, whereas the SIFT model is used for images. Since both deep learning and machine learning models have been considered for face recognition, their performance varied as per model when we used different videos and images. We have demonstrated our proposed model using real-time videos and images using the above technical approaches. LBPH efficiently detected and categorize local characteristics with an accuracy of 99.9%, whereas SIFT consistently maintained an accuracy rate of 88.9%. As our comparative observation, we found that the ResNet model performed well compared to other models.

articleTitle: On the Analysis of a BERT-based Domain-Specific Question Answering Models for Indian Legal System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: The Indian legal system is too large and complex which includes the largest Constitution in the world, thousands of laws, central laws, thousands of acts and many bilateral, regional, and multilateral treaties and agreements with different countries. This makes it difficult to understand and memorize the contents for legal professionals as well as the general public. Some individuals and government officials take advantage of this fact by doing unlawful acts and avoid punishments due to the unawareness in public. So, we are developing a closed domain extractive model for question answering on the Indian legal system. The motivation behind developing a Question Answering System (QAS) on Indian laws is to enhance the accessibility of legal information for both legal professionals and the general public. PDFs of legal acts were collected from the Government website from which Question Answering dataset was created. Dataset contains automatic system generated questions using T5 question generated model and then manual cleaning such as removing wrong questions, minor changes were done. Models used for QA are DistilBERT, RoBERTa, BERT Large. BERT Large outperforms the other models with cosine similarity of 0.944, BLEU score of 0.781, Exact match(EM) with 0.72. Question answering model provides short and precise answers of the questions with context from which the answer was extracted to avoid giving wrong information.

articleTitle: Optimization of PEMFC Fuel Cell Parameters Using Metaheuristic Methods for Efficient and Sustainable Hydrogen Energy Production
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: The increasing importance of renewable energies in the context of the global energy transition highlights the need to refine associated technologies, such as hydrogen fuel cells. To maximize their efficiency and reliability, it is crucial to accurately extract the empirical parameters of fuel cell models, including proton exchange membrane (PEM) models. This task is particularly challenging due to the non-linearity and complexity of the models used. Metaheuristic methods have emerged as promising solutions to address these challenges, offering enhanced capabilities for solving complex optimization problems. Among these methods, the Differential Evolution- Based Backtracking Search Algorithm (DEBSA) stands out for its ability to combine the strengths of two powerful approaches: the Backtracking Search Optimization Algorithm (BSA) and Differential Evolution (DE). DEBSA leverages BSA to guide the exploration of the search space based on past experiences, while DE accelerates convergence towards optimal solutions. This study assesses the effectiveness of DEBSA for parameter extraction in a complex BCS 500W fuel cell model, comparing it with five other well-established metaheuristic algorithms. The results show that DEBSA outperforms the other methods by achieving the lowest sum of squared errors (SSE) and the smallest standard deviation. These performances not only attest to DEBSA’s exceptional precision and stability but also its ability to provide accurate modeling of hydrogen fuel cell behavior. Overall, DEBSA proves to be a highly effective tool for optimizing the parameters of fuel cell models. Its superior performance compared to other algorithms demonstrates its potential to advance parameter estimation techniques and enhance the development of renewable energy technologies.

articleTitle: Synergies and Conflicts: Evaluating AI and 5G Technologies Role in Saudi Arabia’s Drought Management Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Symposium on Advanced Electrical and Communication Technologies (ISAECT)
abstract: Water scarcity across the world and specifically in Saudi Arabia is exacerbated by climatic conditions such as desalinated resources, limited rainfall, reliance on ground water and arid climate. For addressing this issue, governments around the globe have implemented numerous measures leveraging advanced technology like AI and 5G for developed drought management systems. This paper aims to evaluate the synergies and conflicts of Saudi Arabi’s national policies with those of international standards (agreements, conventions and SDGs). The methodology of this paper is based on qualitative content analysis of Saudi Arabia’s policies (Mission 2030, National Innovation Plan and National Water Management Strategy 2030) with those of international agreements (Paris Agreement, UN Convention for combatting desertification & GPAI framework) and SDGs (6, 9, and 13). Python tools and libraries (pandas, nltk, sklearn, OpenPyXL and Networkx) are used for data processing, keyword extraction, themes identification, results extraction and their representation. The intersection of extracted themes has provided results that Mission 2030 and drought management strategy of KSA perfectly aligns with all the selected international agreements and SDGs. However, National Water Strategy 2030 merely aligns with UN Convention and SDG 6. On the other hand, National Innovation Plan of KSA overlaps with the themes of UN Convention, GPAI, SDG 13 and SDG 6 in a perfect manner. The analysis has shed clear light on the KSA’s policies alignment with international standards forecasting the Mission 2030 and drought management strategy in it. Even though the National Water Strategy aligns with merely two standards, it could be a limitation due to limited data set, thematic levels and keyword extraction instead of full text document analysis.
